title: A $40 Doorway Pull-Up Bar Beats Half a Gym Membership
description: A doorway pull-up bar costs less than one month of gym fees and covers back, biceps and core. How to pick one, where to hang it, and what to do at zero reps.
excerpt: The cheapest piece of home gear with the best return — if you know how to use it.
content:
A doorway pull-up bar is still the best value purchase in home training. It costs about forty dollars, takes up zero floor space, and covers the one thing home workouts usually miss: pulling. Push-ups and squats need no equipment. Your back does.

## Pick the right type

There are two. Pressure-mounted bars wedge into the frame by friction — fast to fit, but don't trust them on soft wood or thin modern partition walls. Leverage bars hook over the frame from the outside and hold with your own weight, which is the safer bet in most flats. Check your door width (usually 24–36 in) and the load rating — skip anything under 220 lb.

Before your first rep, hang your full weight on it a few inches off the floor and bounce a little. If it holds that, it holds you.

## If you can't do a single one

That's normal, and the fix isn't "keep trying". Do this instead:

1. **Dead hangs** — just hang, 3 × 20 seconds. Builds grip and teaches your shoulders to stay packed.
2. **Negatives** — jump to the top and lower for 5 seconds. 4 × 3. This is the fastest-working piece.
3. **Inverted rows** — bar low or under a table, body angled, pull to the chest. 4 × 10.

Three weeks of that and the first rep almost always shows up.

## The detail that matters

Overhand grip at shoulder width plus a palm, not a foot wider. Wide grips look hard but shorten the range and load the shoulder joint. And pull your shoulder blades down before your arms do anything — otherwise you've built a biceps exercise.

No good doorway at home, or you want a proper bar with no compromises? An hourly private gym like [GymHome](https://gymhome.cz) solves that for the price of two coffees.
